title: Sticky session failover and transparent retry attenuator for hosted API during customer escalations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During an ongoing customer escalation (large tenant migration), we observed correlated 5xx/timeouts originating from a combination of: an edge sticky-session behavior that routed long-lived streaming connections to overloaded serving nodes, a mismatch between SDK retry semantics and server-side idempotency protections, and a mis-configured circuit-breaker threshold that caused rapid circuit cycling and retry amplification. Impact: multiple high-value tenants experienced elevated error rates and client visible timeouts for synchronous generation requests and streaming sessions.

Root cause hypothesis (consolidated):
- Edge sticky routing (designed to reduce cold KV cache misses) kept certain tenant flows pinned to saturated inference lanes.
- When a backend hit transient saturation it returned 502/504; client SDK retries (4x aggressive retries with no jitter) caused immediate retry storms back to the same pinned nodes.
- Circuit-breaker thresholds were too aggressive (short window, low request-count floor) causing circuits to open/close frequently, producing more 5xx and resetting warm caches.
- Dedicated vs Hosted difference: Dedicated pools had stronger isolation but shared control plane settings inherited a global retry recommendation that was too aggressive for hosted multi-tenant edge.

Goal / acceptance criteria:
- Mitigate customer-visible errors within the next 72 hours using safe server-side controls and a targeted SDK patch where required.
- Restore graceful degradation so affected tenants see rate-limited or slower responses rather than 5xx cascades.
- Implement long-term fixes (per-tenant hysteresis for retries, sticky routing softening, and aligned idempotency guard) with telemetry showing 90% reduction in tenant-originated 5xx during similar load profiles.

Immediate mitigation plan (hotpatches):
1) Edge-routing soft failover: introduce a short TTL (30s) for sticky session affinity on streaming lanes and prefer regional replica after first backend error. This reduces likelihood retries hit same saturated host. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-router/pull/1284)
2) Server-side retry attenuator: add request-level transient-retry quota that declines retry attempts when backend error rate or queue latency exceeds threshold; returns 429 with Retry-After when appropriate to signal client backoff. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-api/pull/4310)
3) Circuit hysteresis tuning: widen the sliding window and add minimum-open duration to prevent flapping. Roll this as a feature flag for quick rollback. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/982)
4) SDK advisory patch: publish a minor SDK release (server-side opt-in header to enable safe-retries) and a guidance note to customers to use idempotency tokens for operations with side effects. (SDK release candidate: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/releases/tag/v0.21.3-rc1)
5) Fast monitoring and alerting: deploy a temporary synthetic workload and Datadog dashboard to compare error rates and tail latency pre/post changes. (Dashboard: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/hosted-api/tenant-escalation-synthetics)

Rollout plan:
- Stage any edge/router changes to 10% of traffic for 30 minutes, monitor for error decrease and CPU/queue impacts.
- Enable server-side retry attenuator in passive mode (log decision only) for 1 hour, then convert to active for affected tenants only.
- Release SDK advisory and coordinate support message to the escalated customers; prepare assisted upgrade where needed.
- If any mitigation increases latency beyond SLO by >15% for >10% of customers, immediately rollback via feature-flag.

Postmortem / follow-ups (medium-term):
- Implement per-tenant retry hysteresis with exponential backoff + jitter and server-side enforcement of idempotency token validation for retryable endpoints.
- Replace hard sticky affinity with cache-aware routing that balances cache-warmth vs load fairness.
- Add unit and integration tests that simulate tenant migration bursts and assert no retry amplification.
- Formalize SDK/server retry semantics in the public docs and add a compatibility matrix for Dedicated vs Hosted defaults.

Notes / constraints:
- We must avoid breaking any existing dedicated-customer guaranteed latency SLAs while adjusting hosted defaults. The feature-flag approach helps staged testing.
- Security review: changes do not add new secrets or key flows. Marked not required for this patch (security_review_required=false).
